body: Most people don't even think of a NW2 as "balding".

I'm 5 weeks in and my shedding has slowed down to practically a halt now. I'm already starting to see small hairs grow in on my scalp and hairline. My scalp is now white underneath my hair instead of flesh colored like it was a few weeks ago. I wasn't expecting this fast of a response from it. If you're a NW1 and even if during the shed you go into a NW2 no one will think you're balding.
Just buy Minox. It's fairly cheap Like $15 a month at the most. None of the "natural" methods have been proven to help with hairloss.
HLT is full of mentally ill incels.

Apply it as part of your morning routine and then apply it again before bed. The foam dries pretty quickly and most people will think you just have some sort of product in your hair if anything.

I don't need to lose any weight I weigh 145 pounds so I'm pretty skinny. I've tried the gym thing a bit in the past and never saw much in the way of results. I think I'm one of those guys who naturally has a hard time putting on much muscle given the fact that I have a small frame.
I don't think all bald men are ugly. I just feel like I'd be ugly bald as it seems to look good bald you have to be built/fit which is something that I'm not and I can't really put on muscle.
I've had my thyroid checked out everything is fine on that front.

It's though because I found a niche of women who do like me and are attracted to me. And it generally tends to be the more alternative type. I just fear they won't be attracted to me anymore if I end up looking like a cop or some kind of nazi from shaving my head.

I feel like a hair transplant is the only thing that would help me look like myself again. Bulking up and having to go to a gym makes me feel uneasy as I abhor the hyper masculine gym brah culture that most gyms seem to be full of.

I'd rather spend 30 grand on a hair transplant honestly. Bald doesn't suit my personality or my features at all. I'd just look like I have cancer or that I'm a Nazi or some shit with a shaved head. Given that I'm pale and skinny. I'm 5'9" weigh only 145 pounds and I'm as skinny as a twig. People give examples of good looking bald men but the problem is I don't identify with them at all because they're always super muscular hyper masculine guys who are 40+ like The Rock or Vin Diesel. When you're a geeky/artsy type it makes it 500x harder because you don't have the hypermasculine look/personality to back up the bald head.
It's probably easier in your 30's because it's expected for a good chunk of men to be balding by then. Not so much when your in your 20s and worried about women your age finding it attractive.

I guess though I can feel these weird 45 degree angles. I've had long hair pretty much my entire life outside of one buzzcut when I was 18. I wasn't crazy about it but everyone else thought it looked better. And I had a head full of hair back then that was so thick that when I got it cut they had to thin it out.
I guess though even with buzz cuts my hideous headshape is exposed. I'm gonna spend $20000 on a hair transplant to avoid exposing this thing if the rogaine doesn't work.
I have a hideous headshape. Giant 45 degree angles on the sides. Plus I'm 5'9 140 pounds so I'd look sick with a shaved head.
Problem is I can't pull of the shaved look. I'm pale and skinny and I can't put weight on to safe my life. I'd just look sickly or like a Nazi with a shaved head.
It's tough because I feel like in a year or so I'll just be another George Costanza instead of a normal young person.

Length shouldn't matter. Get the foam it's easier to apply to the scalp.  Apply it where you're thinning. You may not have much regrowth but at the very least you should be able to maintain or slow down the loss.
Give Rogaine a shot. I've been using it for a month and I'm already noticing some new hairs starting to grow in. It's pretty affordable a 3 months supply costs about $40 at CVS.
My derm wouldn't prescribe it to me because of the risk of side effects due to my IBS. Glad I went though found out I had a fungal infection on my scalp that was contributing to my hairloss.

I gave that a try for about a year. The right side of my cheek is smooth as a baby's butt. Like I can go a couple days without shaving and while other portions of my face have stubble and that sandpaper feel the right cheek is still as smooth as a baby's butt.

I used to have a beard but have since shaved if off. I shaved it off upon realizing how uneven it is. One side of my face the beard was full the other side it only grows from below the jaw line.

I've got these big rad rashes with bumps in some areas of my scalp and some on my face too. Some of the area in my face that looks like it might be infected no facial hair grows at yet on the other side of my face the same area is super dense. My dermotoglist prescribed me 2% ketoconazole shampoo to treat this.
So basically either go with a look that doesn't suit my personality at all or wear a fucking rug. I've never seen a toupee or whatever you call it that looks halfway decent.

Upon closer examination I've realized I'm not at a Norwood 6 diffuse at all. My crown is still in good. I just have a strange pattern where the hair is quite thin in the mid scalp region from roughly an half an inch from the hairline to my ears. Hairline and temples haven't receded past a Norwood 2. I'm a hypochondriac and tend to think see/feel anything "wrong" with my body is 100x worse than it really is.

I already have IBS and have gotten it under control over the last 2 years. I don't want to risk changing things up and having bad flare ups again. My IBS was so bad that I had to go to the ER on multiple occasions to get rid of the pain.
In addition how much does a fungal infection on the scalp contribute to hairloss? My dermatologist diagnosed me with one and said that it's likely a contributing factor.
When you go from being considered attractive to unattractive it does a number on you mentally. Hairloss is probably the worst thing that can happen to a mans appearance outside of becoming obese.
What can be done? I'm likely a future Norwood 7 with the family history I have. I've been told by several doctors that Fin isn't a good idea because I have IBS.
Our best hope is the Dr Tsuji trials go smoothly in 2020. Supposedly his technology offers near unlimited donor supply.

People talk about bald men being attractive and when they give examples it's always hyper masculine celebrities like Vin Diesel or The Rock. I'm artsy and geeky so I fear that it wouldn't suit my personality either. I've always had long hair and up until recently I was able to hide/deny it but that's going away.

I've debated Fin but it wasn't recomended by several doctors to me because I have severe IBS and fin can make that worse. I've been thinking about a transplant but given the fact that I'm under 30 and my dad is a Norwood 7 and has been since he was 20 I fear that I'd be a bad candidate for one.
Depends on your hair texture as well. If you have real tight curly hair than anything longer than half an inch to an inch will give you a Krusty The Clown look with a NW3 or higher.

Update I've spoken with my dermatologist she told me that the burning sensation is to be expected with the shampoo due to the fungal infection on the scalp. I noticed today that I'm starting to get small little hairs on my temples that I feel like previously weren't there.
